historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgement: 10-year average of the base growth path (trough-to-mid-cycle recovery on the continuing portfolio), NOT a historical CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: All historical CAGRs describe a different, larger company: FY23-FY26 revenue -10.9%/yr and FY21-FY26 -5.9%/yr are driven by the Construction (VINCI), Tradelink and steel divestments, not by organic decline; EPS 5-yr CAGR is undefined (FY21 37c -> FY26 21.2c on a share count that rose 824m -> 1,075m through the Nov-2024 equity raise, and FY24-FY25 EPS were negative); owner-FCF FCF 5-yr CAGR from FY21 (peak 658 reported, ~440 owner) to FY26 (124) is -22.5% and reflects the trough. Equity CAGR (+2.3-2.5%) is flattered by the NZ$679m raise. None is a usable forward anchor; the driver paths are built from the continuing-ops FY26 base and the cycle.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series used for the FCF CAGR = reported FCF (OCF - capex) - lease principal - lease interest - interest income - SBC. Lease cash is ~NZ$260m/yr, which is why the owner-FCF history is far below the reported series in every year (FY26: 124 vs 427).

scenario_narratives.base: Trough-to-mid-cycle recovery on the continuing portfolio (Light Building Products, Heavy Building Materials, Distribution, Residential & Development): flat FY27 as guided (softer 1H, commercial delays, residential volumes below pcp), +5% in FY28-29 as NZ residential and civil demand recovers from CY2027, then GDP-like growth. Pre-IFRS-16 EBIT margin rebuilds from ~6% (FY26 ex property gains) to ~8% mid-cycle by FY31-32, cash tax normalises to 28% by FY30, capex ~3% of revenue after the FY27 NZ$170m guide, and a 1%-of-revenue significant-items leakage is charged every year. Terminal value bound by the 13x FCF cap.
scenario_narratives.bull: Cycle turns on schedule and the ROIC programme delivers: FY28-29 revenue +8%/+7% with operating leverage, cost-out and capacity investments (Taupo, Firth, Sonata) lift the pre-IFRS-16 EBIT margin to ~9.5% by FY32, legacy charges fade to 0.5% of revenue, dividends resume, and the Residential & Development review crystallises value at or above its in-model worth.
scenario_narratives.bear: The recovery slips and the legacy tail persists: FY27 revenue -4% then a slow crawl, margin stuck at the ~6% trough level, and significant items keep running at 1.75% of revenue (Iplex 15-year window, retained construction provisions, SkyCity NZICC NZ$330m claim). ROIC never clears WACC; the equity is worth roughly the balance-sheet-adjusted value of a sub-hurdle asset base.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A cyclical building-materials manufacturer/distributor at a construction trough, valued on normalised (mid-cycle) owner FCF of the continuing portfolio only, with leases treated as operating cost, a recurring significant-items haircut inside the margin, cash tax ramped to statutory, a single NZD WACC of 9.5%, and a 13x FCF terminal cap. All values are computed in NZD and converted to the AUD quote at 0.806. Historical CAGRs are reported but explicitly not used: they describe the pre-divestiture group and the FY24-25 distress.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle margin assumption (~8% pre-IFRS-16 EBIT in base) may be too high if the FY26 trough is the new normal for a portfolio still earning 5% ROIC

Recurring significant items: a fresh NZ$250m+ legacy charge (SkyCity NZICC NZ$330m claim, Iplex 15-year window, retained construction provisions) is worth ~NZ$0.20-0.25/share each time and is only partly captured by the 1%/yr leakage
Cycle timing: management's CY2027 recovery is a forecast, and 1H FY27 is already flagged softer; every year of delay pushes the ramp out
Lease-heavy structure (NZ$1.2bn of liabilities) means the ex-lease EV/EBITDA looks cheap on post-IFRS-16 EBITDA -- compare only against EBITDA less the NZ$231m lease cash
Residential & Development strategic review could crystallise value above the in-model worth (upside) or be sold at a distressed price to fund debt reduction (downside)
AUD/NZD translation: the ASX holder is exposed to the NZD IV moving with the cross; 0.806 is the 2026-09-22 rate
Capital notes: 49m dilutive shares on conversion are carried as debt instead; a conversion would move value from the debt line to the share count with no net change

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for FBU.AX at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range A$2.22-3.44. Parity against FBU.NZ (NZX primary) at NZDAUD=X 0.806, see inputs.fx_note.
data_sources.financials: FBU.AX_Metrics.csv / core_metrics (FY2015-FY2026 + 5 half-years); FY2026 Annual Report (signed 18-Aug-2026): income statement, cash-flow statement, note 2.2/2.4 (Significant Items, discontinued ops, held for sale), segment income-statement and cash-flow notes, note 4 (EPS/dilution), note 5 (D&A split incl. right-of-use), note 14/15 (borrowings, funding costs), note 18 (shares on issue), note 26 (share-based payments).
data_sources.qualitative: FBU.AX_Analysis.json (2026-09-22): guidance block (FY27 capex ~NZ$170m, 1H FY27 softer, NZ recovery not before CY2027, dividend reset conditions), bull/bear cases, risk register (Iplex, SkyCity NZICC, retained legacy construction liabilities).

inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report note 26 / statement of changes in equity: movement in share-based payment reserve NZ$7m (vested share-based payment 7). No net-share-settlement tax line disclosed; SBC is immaterial (0.1% of revenue). Kept as an explicit 0.1% row per the SBC-visible house rule.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows in NZD; ASX quote in AUD. NZDAUD=X 0.806 (Yahoo Finance, 2026-09-22T10:47Z). Parity check against the primary NZX listing at the same date: the FBU.NZ regular close x 0.806 ties to the FBU.AX close at inputs.price_as_of within 0.8%, confirming rate direction and quote basis. All per-share values are computed in NZD and converted at 0.806 into the unsuffixed (quote-currency) keys; refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate.
inputs.share_count_basis: 1,075,561,767 ordinary shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (FY26 AR note 18). The diluted EPS denominator (1,124m) adds 49m shares for conversion of the capital notes; those notes are carried inside total_debt (789m includes capital notes), so using the diluted count as well would charge them twice. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows; no buyback programme (buyback_cash 0 for FY24-FY26) so the flat count is a modelling convention the company has not paid for. The Nov-2024 NZ$700m raise (783m -> 1,075m shares) is fully reflected in the current count; no further non-SBC issuance assumed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in NZD, the currency of the flows: NZ 10-yr government ~4.5%, ERP 5.5%, beta ~1.2 for a leveraged building-materials cyclical -> cost of equity ~11%; after-tax cost of debt ~5% (funding costs NZ$64m on ~NZ$900m average gross debt, 28% tax); weights ~86/14 at ~NZ$3.9bn market cap (at the valuation-date price) vs NZ$637m net debt -> ~10.2%, rounded down to 9.5% because cyclicality, the recurring significant-items pattern and litigation risk are charged in the flows (a 1.0% of revenue normalised significant-items leakage inside the EBITDA margin, a 30% bear weight) and not again in the discount rate. One WACC for all three scenarios (adaptations rule f).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. The full continuing-ops lease cash charge (principal NZ$196m + interest NZ$68m group; NZ$231m continuing per the segment cash-flow note) is deducted inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path = 3.85% of revenue, and lease liabilities (NZ$1,235m) are EXCLUDED from net debt. ebitda_margin_path is therefore the post-IFRS-16 EBITDA before Significant Items (FY26 continuing NZ$730m, 12.2%); da_pct_path is D&A EX right-of-use depreciation (316 - 167 = 149, 2.5%) so the lease is charged once and cash-tax EBIT is not understated. Cross-check: ROU depreciation 167 + lease interest 61 = 228 in the P&L vs 231 cash.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (NZ$8m of FY26 earnings, NZ$5m book equity). Flows are left whole and the NZ$5m NCI stock is deducted once in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF with mid-cycle (normalised) margins, per dcf-methods SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical' plus owner-fcf-adaptations.md (currency a1/a2, leases b, NCI c, risk-once f). Same family as BSL.AX and BAP.AX. Independent build for the ASX quote; not copied from FBU.NZ. WHY MID-CYCLE: NZ/AU construction is at a multi-year trough (management: meaningful NZ recovery not before CY2027; 1H FY27 flagged softer); FY26 continuing EBIT before SI of NZ$414m (6.9%) includes ~NZ$52m of surplus-property gains, so the underlying trough margin is ~6.0%, against ~10-11% on the comparable divisions at the FY22-23 peak. Base ramps the pre-IFRS-16 EBIT margin from ~6.3% to ~8% mid-cycle by FY31; bull to ~9.5%; bear stays ~6%. BASE IS THE CONTINUING PORTFOLIO ONLY: base_revenue 5,994 is FY26 continuing operations (Light Building Products, Heavy Building Materials, Distribution, Residential & Development); Construction (sold to VINCI 29-May-2026), Tradelink, Reinforcing/Wire, CSP Pacific and Vivid Living are all discontinued and excluded, so pre-FY2025 group growth rates are NOT used for projection. RECURRING SIGNIFICANT ITEMS: ten-year sum of Significant Items is -NZ$2,291m (FY17-FY26), ~2.9% of revenue per year on the old group; much of it was Construction, but Iplex Pro-fit (15-year claims window, NZ$10m of new legal cost in FY26), retained legacy construction provisions (NZ$73m in FY26), asbestos/silicosis and the SkyCity NZICC claim (NZ$330m) stay with the parent. The ebitda_margin_path is therefore NET of a normalised 'surprise charge' leakage of 1.0% of revenue in base (~NZ$60m/yr), 0.5% in bull, 1.75% in bear -- a haircut, not a one-off. OWNER FCF FY26 (group, for last_fcf): reported OCF 715 - capex 317 (288 PPE/intangibles + 24 mining/stripping + 5 investment property) - lease principal 196 - lease interest 68 - interest income 3 - SBC 7 = 124; this is after a ~NZ$2m net tax refund (tax losses), NZ$58m of significant-items cash outflows and includes discontinued ops, so the projection is component-built and does not carry it forward. reported_fcf 427 = OCF 715 - PPE capex 288 (context-script definition). CASH TAX: near zero in FY26 on carried-forward losses (P&L rate 16.5%); ramped 8 -> 16 -> 22 -> 28% (NZ statutory; AU 30%) by FY30. WORKING CAPITAL: manufacturer/distributor with receivables + inventory > payables; wc_capture -8% of the revenue change (growth consumes cash). CAPEX: FY27 guided ~NZ$170m (2.8%), normalised to 3.0% vs owned D&A 2.5%. TERMINAL: cap 13x FCF for a building-materials cyclical (method: 12-15x); cap binds in base and bull at 9.5% WACC / 2.5% g. NET DEBT: company definition NZ$637m = borrowings 789 (691 non-current + 98 current, includes capital notes) - cash 152 (incl. 7 held for sale); lease liabilities excluded under treatment B. RESIDENTIAL & DEVELOPMENT strategic review (market talk ~NZ$850m) is inside the continuing flows and NOT separately added; a sale at that price would be a bull-case upside of ~NZ$0.15-0.25/share over its in-model value. SBC-light market: house/street band is ~0.1% of revenue wide and near-degenerate. Price is the ASX regular close at inputs.price_as_of, not an after-hours print.

bear.ebitda_margin_note: 1.75% significant-items leakage (the ten-year average was ~2.9% on the old group) and no margin recovery beyond ~6% pre-IFRS-16 EBIT (10.6 - 3.85 - 2.5 = 4.25% after leakage): the FY26 trough proves to be the mid-cycle for a sub-WACC-ROIC portfolio.
bear.narrative: The recovery slips: NZ construction stays subdued past CY2027, 1H FY27 commercial cancellations extend, FY27 revenue -4%, Distribution stays at ~1% ROIC, and the legacy tail keeps paying out -- Iplex claims, retained construction provisions, an adverse or settled SkyCity NZICC outcome -- at ~1.75% of revenue a year. No dividend is resumed within the horizon; net debt stays mid-range.

base.ebitda_margin_note: Post-IFRS-16 EBITDA before Significant Items, NET of a 1.0%-of-revenue normalised significant-items leakage. FY26 actual 12.2% (11.3% ex ~52m property gains); FY27 10.3% = 11.3 - 1.0 with the softer 1H FY27 and input-cost pressure holding margin flat; ramps to 13.3% by FY32 = mid-cycle pre-IFRS-16 EBIT ~8% (13.3 - 3.85 lease - 2.5 D&A = 6.95% after the 1.0% leakage) vs 6.0% FY26 trough and ~10-11% FY22-23 peak.
base.narrative: Trough-to-mid-cycle recovery on the simplified portfolio: FY27 flat (1H softer, NZ residential/civil recovery from CY2027), FY28-FY29 +5% volume-led recovery, then GDP-like growth. Margin recovers to a mid-cycle ~8% pre-IFRS-16 EBIT by FY31-32, never to the FY22-23 peak. Cash tax normalises to 28% by FY30. Capex settles at ~3% of revenue after the FY27 NZ$170m guide. A 1%-of-revenue legacy-liability leakage persists throughout.

bull.ebitda_margin_note: Same construction as base but with a 0.5% significant-items leakage and a ~9.5% mid-cycle pre-IFRS-16 EBIT margin (15.3 - 3.85 - 2.5 = 8.95% after leakage), i.e. the ROIC programme and the cost-out (~NZ$45m SG&A/warehouse savings) deliver and the cycle turns in CY2027 as guided.
bull.narrative: The turnaround works: NZ residential and civil demand recovers from CY2027 with operating leverage on a lower cost base, Distribution is fixed or exited above book, the ROIC programme lifts returns above WACC, legacy items shrink to ~0.5% of revenue and the Residential & Development review crystallises value at or above its in-model worth. Revenue +8%/+7% in FY28-29, margins toward the FY22-23 divisional peak by FY32.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 13x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear lifted from the 15% house default to 30% because the turnaround is unproven (Group ROIC 5.3%, 4.7% ex property, still below WACC; Distribution 1.4%), the Significant Items pattern is recurring rather than one-off (ten-year sum -NZ$2.3bn, five years of NZ$250m+ charges), and the NZ$330m SkyCity claim plus the 15-year Iplex window are open. Bull cut to 20% because it needs three independent things -- the CY2027 cycle turn, the margin rebuild AND no fresh legacy hit -- to all land. Base 50%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
